The article offers a comprehensive overview of the h2 equation, along with related theoretical insights and practical considerations for its application. This specific equation, often referred to as the 'happiest little song,' has numerous advantageous characteristics that make it a valuable tool in engineering, particularly due to its ability to model phenomena without requiring complex numerical methods or accounting for numerical diffusion. The theoretical foundation of this equation is well-established, stemming from conservative form transformation, a concept that was rigorously proven in1983. The characteristics of this equation are simple and two-dimensional, whereas its sources are diverse and wide-ranging. The application of this equation is widespread, with examples including 1982 being the year of its initial use for synthetic voice generation, followed by its utilization in computer graphics for simulating puddles in Gamecube's Rainbow Six game in2003, and its recentimplementation in mobile games for water level simulations.

One key challenge in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) is the problem of mistaken relationships being identified. Current approaches employing global object detectors often label unrelated objects as having no relationship, resulting in a high rate of false negatives. To address this, we introduce an novel framework called Local Context-aware Negative VRL (LCN-VR), a two-stage model. It combines standard global features with locally-derived cues to accurately recognize relationships and detect problematic connections in the scene. Our method is straightforward to implement and effectively mitigates false positives in VRD. Experimental results on COCO and VCOCO datasets show a substantial improvement, yielding a substantial gain of 27.8 and 20.4 in mAP for false positives related detection. Our code has been made available for review at https://github.com/zhengzhengli/LocalContextAwareNegativeVR.

A novel approach has been developed to evaluate the price of quantum correlation in quantum systems. Using this strategy, the price of correlation in quantum dynamics has been successfully applied to analyze the weak measurement process. An newly-defined metric, the weak measurement-based quantum correlation (WMQC), has been proposed and shown to comply with the no-signaling principle. Furthermore, the price of quantum correlation in dynamics has been used to distinguish different states of quantum correlation, including those that are indistinguishable by traditional measures. Unlike prior methods, the price of quantum correlation in dynamics can detect local depletion of quantum correlation even in the presence of Markovian environments. Using this method, the price of quantum correlation in dynamics has been applied to explore the price of entanglement generated or consumed during weak measurement processes in different scenarios. These scenarios involve both entangled and non-local states, and the method has been shown to identify entanglement depletion beyond the limits of traditional measures.

In the fields of vision and language, graph learning has emerged as a field, with applications such as detecting objects, recognizing their attributes, and understanding relationships, like person Person A is the partner of Person B. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to extracting social relationship graphs from images and albums. It involves simultaneously identifying and categorizing individuals and their interconnections within an image. To this end, we developed a two-stage, AI-based system. In the first stage, an image encoder was used to process individual photos and extract features representing person person within each image. In the second stage, an album processor was employed to process a sequence of images and estimate the strength of the connections between individuals. This two-stage method enables the system to effectively leverage visual content from images and the structural information from album layouts to improve the accuracy of the extracted social relationships. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, we created a large-scale dataset consisting of personal photo albums from Facebook users. This dataset, known as the RSSG dataset, was designed to evaluate the performance of relationship extraction models on a real-world scale. Experimentally, we found that the proposed approach demonstrated superior performance compared to baseline methods on the RSSG dataset.

Deep learning models have seen significant success in computer vision, but they face challenges related to very deep network structures, including very long training times and highly static frameworks. In nature, animals successfully process information by rapidly exchanging data, a concept that has been underutilized in deep learning. Very long connections in traditional deep learning models impede the dynamic exchange of information, leading to inefficiencies. This paper introduces dynamic graph communication passing networks, which enable a more organic approach to deep learning by accelerating data transmission and model optimization. Our innovative framework, applied to convoluted neural networks, has demonstrated significant improvements, yielding up to a 2.5x reduction in training time and 5.5x faster inference on public image classification and detection datasets, with minimal to no accuracy loss.

Optimized hardware is often required to implement digital circuits with efficient constant multiplications. Traditional approaches transform the operation into general multiplications or constant multiplications by a power of two, utilizing optimized adder trees. An alternative approach, proposed in this paper, minimizes the need for optimized adder trees. The new strategy reinterprets each constant multiplication as a set of weighted bit additions, significantly reducing the number of additions and adding operations. These additions involve summing scaled versions of individual input bits with corresponding weights. To accelerate these additions, the paper proposes two algorithms for computing multiple weighted bit additions in parallel. The first algorithm assumes the processor registers can store bits and utilizes multiple operations to calculate the total. The second algorithm, which does not rely on optimized adder trees, calculates the total based on the most significant bit of the input. The paper evaluates the proposed method's effectiveness and demonstrates its potential advantages.

Quantum machine learning has emerged as a cutting-edge approach, aiming to leverage quantum computing's unique properties for designing more efficient algorithms, especially for handling complex, large-scale datasets. Among its key areas is quantum neural computation, which applies principles from quantum physics to create more advanced versions of classical neural networks. This work provides an in-depth overview of quantum neural networks, covering their underlying concepts, various applications, and key challenges. Specifically, it covers the use of quantum computing's linear algebra capabilities for quantum neural models, detailed implementations including quantum backpropagation, the benefits of hybrid approaches, and highlights essential research hurdles. By summarizing these issues, we hope to offer a clear path for future research in quantum neural computation, its practical applications, and potential benefits.

The RF accelerator technology forms the core of nearly all particle and nuclear physics research, playing a crucial role in nearly every experiment. Despite being the most mature component of accelerator technology, continuous innovation in this area has the potential to significantly impact the research program at high energy centers, making it the driving force behind further advancement. Therefore, ongoing research into new RF power amplifiers, low-loss cavities, and efficient power recycling will be driving innovation within the field. Additionally, developments in RF power supply, accelerator magnet, and kerf tube research could also contribute significantly. Moreover, the private sector is increasingly investing in RF technology due to its applications in 5G, radar, national security, and aerospace industries, creating new opportunities and demands in RF acceleration technology. The Snowmass RFTG will soon submit its strategy and upcoming challenges in RF technology to the main RFTG report.

A unique position is held by the muon collider among particle collider designs, with its distinct characteristics leading to both significant challenges and exciting possibilities. The rapid decay of muons creates urgency in accelerator design, while also offering high collision rates and reduced detector requirements. The design of future muon colliders has progressed through several key areas, encompassing accelerator technology, muon detectors, and theoretical and experimental analysis of collutions. Recent breakthroughs in negative muon production, absorption, and muon cooling have provided crucial insights into feasible collider designs. The paper provides an overview of recent advancements and recommended pathways for further research on optimal muon collider designs.

The genre of linearized wave dynamics within a relativistic fluid is explored, 
with particular focus on how shockwave formation and propagation are influenced 
by viscosity. We demonstrate that nonlinear interaction between waves is a direct 
result of viscosity, yet the direction of these wave interactions is independent 
of whether the fluid is following the Mubuchi-Ressler-Hull-Fuller hydrodynamics 
or Navier-Stokes theory. We examine both right and left moving waves, 
calculating their speeds and attenuation rates, and make use of numerical methods 
to obtain precise solutions for the wave dynamics, which are then used to analyze 
how the wave interactions evolve over time.

A theoretical model proposes that the observed gamma-ray background in the MeV range from the Compton Gamma-Ray Blind Area could be a byproduct of initial black holes formed right after the Big Bang, specifically named primordial black holes (PBHs). These black holes hold the key to understanding the dark matter puzzle and the creation of neutrino supernova bursts. When PBHs decay, they release a vast amount of energy, including high-energy neutrinos, which interact with the surrounding neutron gas, producing a gamma-ray signal that matches the observed Earth sky background. In this process, the rate of neutrino emission is directly proportional to the density of dark matter and can be calculated based on the PBH mass, which is approximately $10^{17}$ grams. Notably, the resulting neutrino flux significantly exceeds the predicted signal from traditional neutron clouds and outperforms the detected Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS-02) data, demonstrating that gamma-ray and neutrino emissions from the PBHs are a realistic possibility.

Our virtual safeguard platform is an innovative solution that ensures secure and trustworthy execution of software, even in an untrusted virtual machine environment. The platform consists of two key components: a proxy compiler and a runtime system, both working in tandem to verify code integrity and prevent unauthorized modifications. Our compiler translates a high-level programming language into a low-level gate circuit while inserting special monitoring codes, and our runtime system acts as an watchdog over the entire program, validating its operations in a hardware-efficient manner. The challenge of performance overhead is addressed by strategically offloading monitoring tasks to less-critical program segments. The performance of our platform has been demonstrated in a five-stage pipeline processor implementation using the tensor network heuristic transformation approach and the FHEVER tool, achieving reasonable gate densities and approximate error rates. The future direction of our platform involves fine-tuning the routing of monitoring codes for a given program using machine learning techniques to optimize both monitoring and overhead performance.

Researchers have sought polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for various general-valued optimization problems. Due to Valiant's classification, valuated constraint satisfaction problems can be categorized into three distinct regions based on their tractability. However, only limited PTAS were known for the specific 'R1 region'. We introduce a new PTAS for problems falling within 'R1 region', even those with limited constraints and individual constraint weights. Our approach builds on Valiant's linear relaxation, but over a finite domain. We show that solving the finite-valued problem is NP-hard, yet remains feasible with reduced arity. Our finite domain PTAS achieves a $O(n^{\epsilon \cdot \text{ar}})$-approximation, where $\epsilon$ approaches zero and $\text{ar}$ represents the sparsity level. This results in a PTAS for problems with linear constraints and sublinear arity, even with negative constraint weights, although we restrict the arity to a constant. Our finite-valued framework may also be useful in other valuation-based optimization problems.

This paper explores unsupervised and few-shot learning approaches for zero-shot task transfer using the capabilities of a previously trained language model, focusing on downstream tasks such as sentiment analysis, product review analysis, and product recommendation. Our study compares few-shot and unsupervised methods, with a specific emphasis on the efficacy of few-shot learning. We contribute to the field by developing a novel few-shot recommendation algorithm, showcasing its superiority over both unsupervised and supervised techniques on benchmark datasets, according to our experiments.

Our proposed technique for weakly-supervised semantic segmentation in urban landscapes uses high-quality hyperspectral image data in place of traditional RGB images. Leveraging the narrow bandwidth of the hyperspectral spectrum, we developed a novel approach to enhance the separation of semantically similar regions. This strategy involves using a small number of hyperspectral image bands as a novel, highly discriminative feature space for the model. For the actual segmentation task, we combine hyperspectral features with RGB image data and employ a model to minimize the difference between predicted and actual contours in the Cityscape dataset, for which human-annotated boundaries are available. While our method utilizes this boundary annotation for training, it can also operate in a fully weakly-supervised manner using only RGB data and hyperspectral features. Experimental results on the Cityscape dataset demonstrate the efficacy of our method in achieving superior segmentation performance in the category intersection over union metric, when compared to comparable techniques.

A white dwarf's properties can be altered significantly by the presence of matter from its surrounding circumstellar disk, created through the disintegration of a planet or small star. Such interactions have been extensively studied through spectroscopic analysis, which reveals that most involved matter exhibits very low rotation rates despite originating from rotating bodies. However, the peculiar properties of the matter rotating around the star in GW Potassios have distinguished it and raised questions about its origin. In order to address these questions, we have taken into consideration various processes that could potentially alter its rotation, such as angular momentum transport mechanisms and magnetic interactions. Our in-depth examination of this matter's rotation has led to the development of 3D hydrodynamic models that simulate its rotation and evolution, and our results suggest that the rotation and chemical composition of this matter could be explained by the complete consumption of a massive planet with strong internal energy sources capable of influencing momentum transfer.

In algorithm analysis, the RAM model is frequently employed, assuming that basic arithmetic operations like addition are executed in the same time frame. However, for inputs of exponential size in relation to the machine word size, the Merkle-advisory overflow time frame may apply, suggesting that more complex arithmetic operations could take longer. We demonstrate that in a specific variant of the RAM model where the machine can perform addition in constant time, it can also execute multiplication, signed division, and the bitwise shift operation in constant time.

Co-training has long been a successful semi-supervised learning method for multi-view data, relying on two significant assumptions: label independence and inter-label supervision. While this approach has been extended to sequential and session-based recommendation, it has been limited to sequence-oriented data, leaving session-based users and their sessions underrepresented. To address this gap, co-training has been adapted for session-based recommendation, but with the restriction to sequence-based users only. To bridge this gap, a novel graph-based co-training framework is introduced, a method that can be applied to both session-based and sequence-based recommendation. Within this framework, two key hypotheses are proposed: session stability and inter-session diversity. A graph co-embedding method is designed to validate these hypotheses, and this method can be self-supervised using link prediction. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework and its feasibility using self-supervision, surpassing state-of-the-art methods.

This research is centered around the concepts of group LCD and group reversible LCM codes within linear code theory, forming an expansion of stable codes in this domain. It defines these codes and examines their essential characteristics and inherent attributes, defining a specific type of quasi-self-dual codes that generate group LCD codes, as well as presenting a method to create group reversible LCM codes using alternative group codes and presenting an example involving the symmetric group on 4 letters.

We define graphs, morphisms, and a differential, creating a differential category in the process. This framework enables the creation of homology, providing a natural basis for Feynman integrals and the amplitudes of amplitund calculations in quantum field theory. Our research reveals that these integrals are not solely dependent on the given amplitude but also on a selected non-singular gauge, an outcome fully demonstrated through an explicit basis in our work. Our framework naturally yields four new relations among amplitund, corresponding to four new irreducible singularity structures in reductions, as demonstrated in a recent preprint. Our framework provides novel insights into the topological properties of graphs and the nature of local and global solutions, demonstrating that these integrals are single-valued functions.

A theory called the category-gradient hypothesis suggests that objects share properties on a continuous scale, with some properties more relevant to categorization than others, and these more relevant properties more strongly guide learning in observers. We investigated this idea in recurrent neural networks, showing that networks trained for object categorization, regardless of the training conditions, adjust their use of object properties so that they rely more on properties more relevant to the category being learned, and we found that the categories learned by these networks can be predicted by the way they use these properties. Furthermore, we found that the way these networks process objects, often along category axes, is similar to some of the ways human neurons process images, and that this characteristic processing style helps them learn new categories. Category-orthogonal object traits may therefore play a crucial role in how the brain processes visual information and learns object categories.

Topologically protected edge states in one-dimensional systems can be stabilized despite instability by using non-Hermitian symmetry, allowing for new classifications and controlling the open-boundary problem. We propose a new approach to gapless topology classification, offering a new definition, definitions for topological invariants applicable to both gapped and point-gap systems and bypassing the need for an infinite system size. Our method defines topological invariants for one-dimensional non-Hermitian point-gap systems by considering correlation functions of local observables and defining a correlator that remains unchanged under system deformations. We demonstrate that for systems with short-range correlations, the correlator can be expressed as a sum of products of local winding numbers. Our classification results are confirmed with various numerical examples.

Research on Golay complementary arrays has been more recent compared to palindromic Golay complementary sets, yet the applications of GCAAs in various fields like sensor arrays have gained significant traction due to their zero side lobes property. Despite available designs of GCAAs being limited to a few cases, this study presents novel methods for constructing GCAA of length $L$ and $p$-arity. The first method involves merging GCAA of lower lengths $L_1$ and $L_2$ with specific values of $p$. The second method derives GCAA from unitary designs, with $p=4$. The third method involves applying a truncation technique on GCAA with $p=4$. The results of these studies have led to the discovery of new GCAA, unlike the existing designs.

A novel method is proposed and studied to enhance comprehension of the Higgs boson's properties and its connections to other vector particles. Off-production measurements of the Higgs boson are utilized to deduce its decay width, while its interactions in off and on-shell states inform us about the Higgs portal to dark matter. This is achievable due to the Higgs boson's similar coupling structure to vector particles, regardless of their mass. The proposed method uses four-lepton decay data from 13 TeV proton-proton collisions, with a combined luminosity of 120 fb^-1, across multiple decay channels. The Higgs boson mass is 125 GeV. The expected precision for off-shell production and decay width measurements is within 5% and 2-3% ranges, respectively. With a few additional luminosity, the LHC is poised to confirm unitary in the VVV sector and potentially reveal non-standard models of Higgs potential.

In this study, we present an innovative approach for comparing two unsupervised changes in multispectral data. Our method involves fusing the features from a multi-scale deep convolutional neuromodulator and aligning them using a linear layer. Our proposed unsupervised change detection model outperforms other well-known models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and the KNN metric when evaluated against the ground truth.

Let $h(G)$ be the smallest number such that any two-coloring of the integers is guaranteed to produce monochromatic copies of the $h(G)$-th set of elements in the semigroup corresponding to any two-coloring-invariant scheme, where at least one copy is formed with homogeneous elements. This element count must be consistent across all colorings. For cases involving the direct sum of squares, we determine that $h(\Box\Box) \le 11$, and based on Schur's theorem, it is clear that $h(\Box\Box) \le 19$, and this number can be reduced to 16 due to the principle of numbers, thus establishing the given inequality. This has implications for Tait's conjecture about the Four-Color Theorem, where it is obvious that $h(\Box) \le 15$, and it is known that $h(\Box) \le 13$. This yields the inequality for Tait's conjecture. In general, it is known that $h(\Box) \le 13$. For the theorem by L. Stockmeyer, it is known that given any two-coloring of the integers, it is possible to find a monochromatic copy of the $h(\Box) \le 13$. This element count must be consistent across all colorings.

Quantum interference is a key element in silicon spin qubit operations which impose a phase on electron wavefunctions. A recent study conducted in graphene revealed that a critical element in this process involves valley interference affected by scattering from carbon atoms. Researchers have now extended their investigation to silicon, examining the influence of silicon dopants on phase accumulation during gate-induced loop movements of electrons. By analyzing the phase shifts across multiple electron charges, researchers discovered that valley interference significantly impacts phase accumulation at the atomic level in silicon, affecting phase shifts caused by at least a few dopants. Given that valley interference plays a crucial role in phase accumulation, researchers have proposed that a new technique, called spin swapping, could be developed to minimize dopant-induced phase errors in future multi-qubit silicon processors.

Nonconvex optimization is a crucial field employed in a broad range of practical applications such as control, neural networks, and bioinformatics. However, the effectiveness of various methods addressing nonconvex problems is often fragmented, with limited comparisons between software implementations. To address this issue, we introduce a unified, flexible framework using Julia that facilitates the swift development and deployment of modern nonconvex optimization algorithms on a comprehensive collection of benchmark problems. Using our framework, we can rapidly create and test multiple solution methods, evaluate their performance on an extensive set of problems, and compare their real-world applicability in multiple domains. The framework's capabilities are illustrated through the integration of 33 state-of-the-art methods and 310 tasks, with the implementation of our techniques contributing significantly to the advancement of nonconvex optimization. As an open-source project hosted on GitHub, our framework, known as LibOPT, can serve as a benchmarking suite, benchmarking problem library, and a ready-to-use implementation of nonconvex optimization algorithms, aiding researchers and practitioners in the optimization community.

In their investigation, the authors establish a critical relationship between a finite group G's ability to act transitively on a G-invariant algebraic shape within a finite-dimensional vector space V. Specifically, they prove that G can act k-times transitively if and only if it acts k times transitively on each irreducible component of the shape. Furthermore, they provide a formula for the maximum transitivity degree, which they denote as deg_G(\Xi), and demonstrate that the family of shapes consists of the minimal set of irreducible shapes with a maximum deg_G of g. Additional results include the definition and calculation of the shape ring, along with an exploration into its finiteness.

The challenge of non-Abelian non-commutative geometry, where spatial coordinates do not commute, is addressed by establishing a rigorous framework for the action of function multiplication and coordinate operation. Specifically, we derive an identity for four non-commuting coordinates in terms of their commutators. Using a specific expansion based on this identity, we express any function of these coordinates in terms of a new set of commuting variables, effectively identifying spacetime with a familiar, commutative manifold. As a consequence, S-matrix calculations for two quantum particles in this non-commutative spacetime can be performed more effectively. Our study reveals that for certain interactions, the non-Abelian effect on spacetime leads to distinct vertex structures, making S-matrix calculations more complex. We demonstrate this phenomenon for a scalar $\lambda \Phi^4$ theory, obtaining explicit expressions for two- and four-boson scattering matrices. Our calculations yield clear conclusions about the impact of non-Abelian geometry on scattering outcomes, with significant differences observed in terms of interaction, frequency, and direction. Our work reveals a striking finding: for two quantum particles, their interactions in non-Abelian spacetime lead to a scattering outcome where they emerge in a different channel, with frequency and direction, than they entered. This channel transformation is more pronounced for four-boson scattering, where we observe scattering between two frequency groups, with a directionality preference. This frequency and direction dependence is more complex for four-boson scattering

Precise control of charge transport is crucial for diamond radiation detectors. This study applies the two-photon absorption transient voltage technique to examine the 3D transport of electrons and holes in high-quality diamond. This advanced pump-probe method uses an intense, pulsed laser to excite carriers in the sample and a continuous probe beam to track voltage changes. This technique has resolved electron and hole movement within millimeter-sized diamond, with probe powers to capture each carrier type's movement separately. We have observed how electrons and holes behave in different oriented channels in the diamond and have determined key mobility and lifetime characteristics. This technique has also enabled us to investigate and model the complex interaction between electrons and holes in the diamond.

Social media platforms are facing significant challenges due to the pervasive issue of hate speech. Classifying this content solely as present or absent is insufficient, given the varied forms and levels of hate speech exist. This study presents an advanced methodology for identifying and categorizing hate speech on Arabic social media, utilizing a comprehensive dataset comprising 12,000 texts, meticulously annotated for both the presence of hate speech and its specific category, as well as its target, i.e., misogyny. The methodology employs a deep neural network that concurrently performs multiple tasks, integrating character-level and word-level embeddings to enhance its character-level performance. This proposed approach surpasses the current state-of-the-art models, demonstrating exceptional outcomes on both the Arabic Twitter dataset, showing improvements of 2.1% in F1-score and 1.8% in accuracy, as well as the Arabic Facebook dataset, with improvements of 2.2% in F1-score and 2.0% in accuracy.

This study aims to solve the given stochastic differential equations, which are set within a fixed time interval, taking the fractional Brownian motion with a parameter less than 0.5 into account. Specifically, we have established the existence and uniqueness of solutions, which is subject to specific conditions, by analyzing the conditions under which the Lipschitz condition can be satisfied. Additionally, we have derived a comparison theorem, which is essential for establishing the Lipschitz condition, and finally, we have illustrated our findings with relevant examples.

We introduce a novel framework for producing adaptable and fault-tolerant control systems. The system consists of a learning-based adaptive controller and a traditional adaptive control regulator, the parameters of which are adjusted using an internal simulation model. The simulation model is refined using a method that prioritizes robustness, and prefers not to alter, an adaptive control regulator already performing well. The parameters of the simulation model are then used to develop an adaptive control regulator that mimics it. This approach allows us to derive analytical guarantees that the resulting adaptive control systems will be robust and will fail safely. The robust parameters of the simulation model can also be used to create adaptive control systems that fail safely and meet specific performance requirements. The proposed strategy is implemented and tested on a mobile robot.

A new framework is proposed to standardize coded caching and distributed computation techniques. It unifies these previously considered distinct approaches under one framework by recognizing their shared Shonhag information retrieval process. This framework is illustrated with examples of rate-storage pairs and decoding complexity for different linear computation and caching protocols. The framework enables new schemes by combining existing ones and optimizes storage and computation requirements. Furthermore, it provides a general decoding method, leading to a lower bound on the storage capacity for linear computation and caching protocols. This framework is straightforward to implement and coherent, making it user-friendly.

We establish the Scott model of continuous semantics in univalent type theory. To achieve this, we develop a comprehensive framework for continuous domains and functions within univalent type theory and demonstrate its equivalence to the existing framework of cpo's and continuous functions, thereby obtaining a full characterization of the Scott model.

This paper focuses on applying Eisenstein series feedback to a specific automorphic form, a lowest-weight Whittaker function, at a critical point of the spherical Hecke algebra within $GL(n)$. Our approach draws from foundational work by Geller and Schuster, incorporating additional techniques and a novel set of sums, termed 'Combinatorics of Heisenberg type,' to facilitate analysis within the Heisenberg group. Additionally, we present key lemmas supporting this analysis.

This research focuses on the secure operation of a mobile robotic arm in the presence of unanticipated obstacles and uncertain positions. To achieve this, we have developed a novel control approach that combines configuration awareness with barrier functions. This approach divides the workspace into distinct regions and generates barrier functions specific to each region, taking into account boundaries between them. We validate our method through simulations of a real-world scenario, controlling a robot arm while collecting and handling objects, and ensuring its safe navigation around obstacles.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study within computer science, strives to comprehend written text and spoken language, enabling a better understanding of human communication. This knowledge can subsequently be applied to generate responsive speech. Despite its long-standing importance, text analysis continues to be a challenging task for computer systems. Among various text analysis methods, summarisation via extraction stands out as a significant approach, aiming to create concise summaries of lengthy texts. This study presents an algorithm for creating textual summaries through extraction, utilizing nodes and edges to represent sentences and their relationships. To determine edge weights, an analysis of sentence lengths and overlap sentences is conducted, with the goal of identifying the most significant connections. Following this, an algorithm is used to identify the nodes with the highest node edge weights.

Researchers have explored the application of Bose-Einstein condensates to nonlinear quantum computation by investigating nonlinear extensions of established quantum model transformations. This research focuses on adapting complex Bose-Einstein condensate functions to simplify the Bose-Hubbard model, and evaluating their effectiveness using quantum measures such as entanglement and circuit complexity. Furthermore, the concept of a C-number approximation to Bogoliubov's approach to BEC is proposed, and its potential to provide a comprehensive understanding of quantum many-body systems is considered.

Consider $F$ and $G$ as meromorphic mappings from a complete K\"{a}hler manifold $M$ to a projective variety $X$, with both mappings sharing the same indeterminacy set and trivial combined indeterminacy. If the closures of their images intersect transversally and $F$ and $G$ dominate an equidimensional family of divisors, with their divisors being equidimensional, and if $F$ and $G$ are sufficiently close, with $G$ being generically finite, then it is inferred that $F$ and $G$ are identical. This conclusion holds as long as the degrees of $F$ and $G$ satisfy the inequality $\deg(F) < \deg(G) \leq 2^{\deg(F)}$. This result extends existing distinctness theorems in the context of Nevanlinna theory, including distinctness theorems for algebraic and transcendental subvarieties.

Polynomial systems with non-degenerate solution counts hold significant importance in multiple disciplines, including computational geometry, kinematics, and geometry with applied purposes. We introduce a method to identify the nondegenerate subset of a given polynomial system's hypersurface. Utilizing signature maps, this algorithm not only computes nondegenerate points but also leverages the connection between signatures and hypersingularities to efficiently detect such points. We integrate a certificate approach with connected component separation techniques from prior work to implement our algorithm. While signature maps are typically employed for global solution isolation, our proposed workflow can be part of a global isolation procedure or applied independently to find nondegenerate points. We demonstrate the feasibility of our algorithm through implementation and provide benchmark results for global isolation and nondegenerate locus computation.

Directly produced photons provide invaluable insight into the underlying processes of particle collisions. Their unique property allows them to escape the collision without being altered, directly linking cross-section to temperature. Researchers at the STAR collaboration used a novel method to calculate a specific ratio, $\phoelphoel$, which is independent of measurement biases and helps determine low-momentum direct photons in Cu$+$Cu collisions at 200 GeV. This technique separates photonic signals from other processes, such as fragmentation, by cross-referencing electron-photon pairs with photon-electron pairs. After correcting for jet fragmentation, researchers found an excess of photons in Cu$+$Cu collisions at 200 GeV, which increases with centrality. This observation aligns with theoretical models of thermal radiation and other theoretical models, such as initial state Scet and final state cascade.

The search for the maximum number of edges in a graph without a specific subgraph is a fundamental problem in extremal combinatorics. This paper provides a solution to this problem for a particular case of the tetrahedron $\K43$, where the graph is required to be free of induced copies of the tetrahedron with three edges of equal length. This problem is a three-dimensional version of a well-known conjecture by Erdos and Simonovits, and it can be seen as an application of the hypergraph regularity method.

To mitigate the Pitfall of line edges becoming blocky and aliased on vector maps due to limited display resolution, methods must be implemented for effective anti-aliasing. This becomes particularly crucial for line joins, as they are often short segments that can be affected more severely. Currently, two main approaches have been used to address this issue: increasing vector map resolution, or applying color filter banks. The first approach, while simple to implement, leads to unnecessary file bloat and potential compatibility issues. The second approach, although avoiding bloat, can introduce color shifts and inconsistencies. This paper introduces a novel anti-aliasing technique focused on effectively handling line joins without altering vector map features, thus achieving a balance between avoiding color shifts and maintaining file size efficiency.

The multivariate interpolation problem is a critical mathematical task with various applications in data interpolation, function approximation, and related fields. This study introduces a novel, transcendental interpolation formula using the exponential function as a basis, which is both a smooth and an oscillating function. This novel interpolation scheme is then used to create global, non-linear, and stable interpolation and approximation operators, including a new quasi-interpolation operator based on the exponential interpolation scheme. The theoretical properties of the resulting operators are analyzed, and numerical experiments validate the proposed operators as efficient alternatives to existing interpolation methods.

We've developed a new method to identify the PWN domains of gamma-ray-emitting pulsars within the Galaxy. By utilizing a sample of 50 pulsars with known neutron star locations, we determined the spatial boundaries of each pulsar's PWN domain. We observed that these PWN domains typically measure around 300 parsecs in size, with typical widths of about 100 parsecs. Based on our findings, we estimate there are approximately 1,200 pulsar domains within the Galaxy's neutron star population. We analyzed various factors that influence the morphology and size of these PWN domains, such as distance from the Galactic plane, and found no evident correlation with these features. We discovered that pulsars emitting both neutron star and PWN gamma-rays are usually surrounded by supernova remnants, and that the penguin-shaped pulsar morphology is associated with the NGC 1098 galactic bar. Based on our analysis of the relationship between pulsar age and energy spectrum index, we found evidence that older pulsars tend to have harder energy spectra, and proposed a novel explanation for this observation involving the role of magnetic reconnection and the magnetic field structure within the pWN.

Classifying images into four categories such as clear weather, foggy conditions,
rain, and snow, poses a significant visual recognition challenge. Due to varying
weather data sets, comparing results across different studies proves difficult. In this research, 
a comprehensive evaluation of numerous deep learning methods is conducted using carefully 
constructed input images to enhance accuracy, along with the newly developed Multi-Class 
Weather dataset, a multi-class image collection featuring clear weather, foggy conditions, 
rain, and snow. The proposed dataset was designed to validate and compare the performance of different 
state-of-the-art deep learning architectures on an uncomplicated multi-class image classification task.
The proposed data augmentation method significantly improves model performance by increasing 
generalizability and reducing the risk of overfitting. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that our 
approach yields better performance than existing solutions for this application, and the proposed 
dataset offers a valuable resource for evaluating and comparing deep neural networks in weather 
image classification.

Global climate change is accelerating, and although necessary measures to mitigate its effects have been identified, they are difficult to implement. This study examines how climate change policies are hindered by discrepancies in societal perceptions and values. To bridge the gap between the science of climate change, institutional policies, and the economy, we apply one health approaches to investigate the interplay of societal standards. By combining interviews with experts in climate science, economics, and institutional policy, we highlight the significance of unresolved societal differences in explaining the inadequate response to climate change. Our research promotes awareness of various societal norms and their interactions to enhance public policy in climate change, promoting more environmentally friendly practices. Ultimately, we advocate incorporating climate friendliness into personal lifestyles to promote better societal standards.

Recent advancements in soft robotics technology, leveraging the flexibility of soft materials, have sparked significant research interest. A key challenge in this field is the limitation of conventional control methods, which, due to the non-linear and complex nature of soft agents, often require model-based approaches that are cumbersome and time-consuming to implement. This paper proposes a novel, model-free control framework, specifically designed for controlling a soft multi-fingered gripper, leveraging the power of the online Koopman operator. By leveraging the kernel trick, this framework simulates the behavior of the gripper in real-time and develops a dynamic model that is adaptable to changing conditions. An optimal control approach is employed to develop a closed-loop control law, which is demonstrated to be effective in accurately gripping objects of various sizes and is shown to be transferable across different soft gripper materials. Furthermore, this framework allows for the formulation of a safety filter, which ensures that the gripper's movement remains within safe bounds and is applicable across different types of soft grippers.

The Organic General Gradient Descent (OGGD) is a broad framework that encompasses conventional General Gradient Descent (GLD) and extends it to address non-convex problems in a more comprehensive manner. Our objective is to further broadens OGGD by relaxing its O-type restriction, which has further relaxed OGDG (R-OGDG) as a previous attempt. However, R-OGDG is shown to fail in achieving global convergence under specific conditions. As a result, we establish convergence on OGGD with even a less strict O-type constraint. Additionally, we propose a new OGGD-BS (Backtracking) variant, which offers several advantages, including the ability to achieve a global convergence rate and ensure the O-type descent condition is met without relying on the strict convexity assumption.

The high-redshift source J2102+6015 at $z$ = 4.575 has been observed in detail using HST, JWST, and LOFAR. This detailed observation enables us to establish that the object has a redshift of 4.575 and that it contains a central, centrally active black hole that is likely a star-forming star-forming galaxy. This high-redshift source exhibits significant UV and IR continuum flux, as well as intense star formation. Lung cancer is a severe illness requiring tailored treatment and accurate diagnosis, which can be supported by advanced technology. The growth and progression of lung cancer can be effectively captured and analyzed by deep learning models, which can also consider factors affecting the disease, such as genetic and molecular characteristics. This research proposes a comprehensive data analysis method that integrates multiple data sources, including clinical information and imaging, to predict the survival rate of non-small cell lung cancer patients. The method employs specific algorithms to analyze and process data and uses neural networks to predict outcomes, which are then fine-tuned to optimize results. To address data imbalance, a specialized weighting system is implemented. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through extensive testing on a large dataset from the National Cancer Institute. The proposed model outperforms current models in predicting patient survival and may support doctors in making informed treatment decisions, potentially contributing to the development of intelligent diagnostic systems.

In numerous real-world applications of reinforcement learning, the intricate nature of the environment makes it challenging or even impossible to derive a simple mathematical model. To overcome this, researchers have developed ReNLaSe, a novel approach that leverages natural language to create a state representation for the environment. This external model can be trained independently using graphical tools and is subsequently utilized as a representation in reinforcement learning. This work provides a comprehensive overview of the ReNLaSe methodology, reviewing its historical background, key characteristics, implementation, both theoretical and empirical assessments, as well as the adoption of natural language in reinforcement learning more broadly.

A novel approach based on machine learning is introduced, for extracting quasar pseudocross-correlation signals from actual data of absorption systems in spectra. The signal is predicted based on binary classifications of individual redshifted absorption features. This method simplifies data requirements, removing the need for aligned spectra and self-prediction. The framework's effectiveness is confirmed by comparing its predictions with established pCS signals from the COS-HIGH sample, providing consistency across all wavelength ranges. The framework's flexibility allows it to incorporate various forest power spectrum estimators by adapting its input. Furthermore, our method can accommodate future large-scale datasets, integrating them into existing surveys without the computational challenges associated with traditional pseudocorrelation estimation.

This research delves into the finite-dimensional representations of key Lie algebras related to the Weyl algebra, specifically those describing symmetric and antisymmetric functions under group actions, and polynomial functions under joint symmetry actions. Building on the classical Schur-Weyl-Duflot decomposition, we aim to establish a general method for a schur-weyl-duflor type decomposition applicable to the aforementioned algebras' representations. As a foundational step, we prove that certain Lie algebras have free modules over themselves, deriving an explicit construction for their Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt bases.

Social media sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter offers valuable insights
into public opinion due to its widespread adoption and expressive nature of
user-generated content. Despite being informative, capturing sentiment on
Twitter is challenging because of sentiment-contrary words, fragmented syntax,
and unique writing styles that include capitalization and punctuation variations.
This study proposes an Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to predict Twitter
sentiment, where each tweet is transformed into a sequence of word embeddings.
The effectiveness of the proposed model is demonstrated on two real-world Twitter
datasets, namely the Kenyans on Twitter and the Twitter Sentiment Analysis
datasets, using standard evaluation metrics. The experimental results indicate
that the proposed model achieved remarkable accuracy of 86.88% and 84.21%,
respectively, in capturing Twitter sentiment.

Role-specific dialogue systems that embody particular characteristics are essential in domains such as education and security, where users seek responses that reflect unique features. Despite this, developing open-domain dialogue systems with defined roles is an unsolved challenge. To address this issue, we propose a novel system featuring an implicit state management mechanism and a strategy to insert role-related elements into generated responses. Our proposed techniques are tested using both a basic character (Einstein) and a complex one (Marilyn Monroe), showcasing the effectiveness of our system in portraying distinct characters. Additionally, our implicit state management outperforms a traditional graph-based system in terms of coherence and consistency, with our role-insertion strategy yielding positive evaluations of both surface-level language quality and deeper semantic relevance.

Newly discovered memory effects in gravitational waves, first detected by the LIGO and Virgo observatories, have the potential to create their own background noise in the detection of future events. This type of background noise is created by the cumulative signal memories from all past mergers that share the same sky location and is difficult to distinguish from the waves themselves. Research has been carried out to quantify the difficulty of detecting future waves in the presence of this type of background noise, and it has found that its effects are significant for the LIGO Band. Specific parameters were determined that describe the background noise, and it was found to be strongest for the most frequent types of mergers, leaving little room for their signals to be visible. The issue is likely to worsen as the number of detected mergers increases and is expected to be most challenging for the most common types of mergers in the high-frequency bands of the LIGO detectors. The situation is anticipated to be most challenging for the most frequent types of mergers and will be most pronounced when their locations are well-established. The issue is likely to be most challenging for the most frequent types of mergers in the high-frequency bands of the LIGO detectors, specifically for the most common types of mergers. Upcoming detectors with wider and more memory-sensitive frequency bands, such as the LIGO Intermediate detector and the LIGO Third detector, are likely to experience even greater difficulties in this regard.

A hypothetical large-hypothesis phase transition could have occurred in the early universe, leading to significant far-reaching effects. This scenario involves multiple benefits including baryon generation through the leptonic process, detection signals through a potential detection of phase transition effects, and the creation of primordial black holes. Our research shows that the energy scale of the phase transition can match the required conditions for baryon generation, while also producing detectable signs of the event. Furthermore, we have discovered that the resulting black holes have characteristics that could be identified through a cosmic observation survey. This study provides a comprehensive framework that can guide further exploration, while also demonstrating the feasibility of testing the theory through a comprehensive analysis of observational data from multiple sources.

To simulate complex dynamics in real-world systems, researchers have created various agent models, each with its own approach. A specific challenge is modeling cognition, which existing models, especially those based on neural networks, find difficult to capture. A novel approach, inspired by sign-based communication, emerges as a promising solution. This paper takes a significant step forward by presenting a neuro-symbolic approach to causal reasoning, designed to learn and communicate about complex systems, which operate under constraints. A dynamic constraint satisfaction system, representing artificial ecosystems, is learned by training and integrated with reasoning capabilities for query analysis and counterfactual assessment. A reasoning agent, equipped with an emergent ability to predict system outcomes, is able to answer questions and generate hypotheses. Furthermore, through a communication system, inspired by signaling games, the agents can learn to describe and report on their observations in the environment.

In the field of Natural Language Processing, term prediction is a crucial task. The objective of term prediction is to identify the missing word in a given text sequence, with potential applications in completing cut-off search queries and filling in narrative gaps. Our study compares two algorithms - a pre-trained word embedding model and an algorithm that combines the strengths of Bayesian conditional independence and the word embedding model - to determine their efficacy in predicting the next term. Our findings indicate that the second approach, which we refer to as a hybrid algorithm, outperforms pre-trained word embedding models by significantly reducing error rates, with variations ranging from 4% to 44% depending on the dataset used.

Session-oriented recommendations are gaining traction in the recommendation field,
as they can propose more accurate and context-aware suggestions by considering a
user's current session. Nevertheless, existing methods face a challenge in
capturing the complex ranking nuances between candidate items, which can
significantly impact recommendation quality. To address this issue, we propose a
novel two-stage session-oriented recommendation framework that incorporates item
rank embeddings from a learning-to-rank model to capture the dynamic progression
of users' session interactions, as well as the evolving ranking preferences during
the session. In the online setting, we adapt the framework using candidate rank
embeddings, allowing the two stages to synergistically contribute to the final
recommendation output. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our
proposed method over state-of-the-art baselines in terms of both hold-set and
online metrics.

In recent years, there's been a surge of fascination with systems that spontaneously generate motion, as they offer a novel framework to explore how molecules behave and form larger structures without external control. From this field, there's emerged a specific type of colloidal molecule, consisting of two attached self-propelling particles, which provides an ideal platform to study the behavior of complex systems. A study was conducted involving a mixture of dimers and particles, where an external force was used to control the distribution of the molecules and simulate their interaction with a cell membrane. The resulting insights could be applied to create targeted functions in the molecule, as well as provide a new tool for studying the behavior of complex systems on a molecular level.

A three-dimensional network of interconnected fractures within a porous medium is modeled, where the flow and transport processes are governed by Darcy's law and a linear advection-dispersion equation, respectively, and a coupled treatment of pressure and concentration fields is enforced. A simulated method of separation is employed to solve these coupled equations, followed by a specialized method for finite elements to ensure consistency and a high-order of accuracy. A method for conforming meshes, applicable to three-dimensional discrete fracture-matrix systems, is presented, where fractures are explicitly parameterized and integrated into a global mesh, and a preliminary study validates the approach's effectiveness in terms of convergence and stability.

This research focuses on maintaining a formation of close-proximity objects, 
which is crucial in various applications such as object transport and entertainment 
shows, but is challenging due to the interplay of gravitational and collision risks.
In this study, we develop an algorithm that guides a swarm of drones to collect, 
transport, and maintain the shape of a regular geometric object, like a square,
while avoiding collisions and stabilizing in an environment affected by gravity.
Using potential fields and an adaptation of the ICP algorithm, we successfully maintain 
a suspended geometric object and prevent collisions with a predefined threshold limit.
Experimental results from simulations validate the effectiveness of our algorithm.

In our investigation of the spectral properties of Seidel matrices for specific graph classes, such as split graphs and co-clique-sums of complete bipartite graphs, we derive general formulas for their range and energy, with the exception of n-vertex chain graphs where explicit energy expressions are provided.

This study tackles a sophisticated optimal control problem that applies a statistical statement to optimize a given objective function, taking into account dynamics influenced by fractional Brownian motion. To solve this problem, we first develop variational equations and covariations for the system, and then derive necessary conditions for optimality using a Lagrange multiplier technique. To further simplify the problem and make it more applicable to a wide range of scenarios, we transform it into a problem that utilizes a mean-field derivative and derive corresponding stationarity conditions. Finally, we demonstrate the convergence of the stationarity conditions to variational equations and necessary conditions for optimality in the limit.

The properties of a one-dimensional, non-self-adjoint Dirac operator with a symmetric potential are being investigated within the framework of elliptic theory, given that its first component satisfies a specific quadratic equation with an elliptic solution. The associated spectral projections are defined for certain areas of the complex plane, leading to the calculation of finite-band elliptic operator spectra. Consequently, formulas for the associated elliptic eigenvalues and trace ell$_{\lambda}$ are derived, namely, the sum of the $\lambda$-th power of the elliptic spectrum. Moreover, as the value of $\lambda$ approaches infinity, the associated trace asymptotics are derived, namely, the for the elliptic version of Weyl's law, we get $\tau_{\lambda}$, the sum of the $\lambda$-th power of the elliptic spectrum.

VRS are a key component in V2X technology, facilitating communication and data collection; however, they have limitations in reach due to spacing intervals. To overcome this constraint, a two-tier network has been proposed that incorporates VRS and vehicle relays, where the latter use DSRC for communication, enabling the coverage of unconnected areas, real-time data transmission, and implementation of applications, including routing, sensor data collection, and traffic modeling. This study develops a mathematical model to calculate traffic flow and vehicle distances, creating a two-tier network, and presents optimization methods to determine optimal placement for VRS and relays, verifying their efficacy through simulations.

The goal of our research is to utilize machine learning to automatically identify and label page edits on Wikipedia that have had a minimal impact on the page's overall quality, allowing us to investigate the effect of low-quality contributors on Wikipedia's content. We developed three distinct sets of edit characteristics, or features, to capture the editing behaviors of contributors from different perspectives. By training our models on this data, we achieved a 70-80% accuracy in automatically identifying low-quality content edits, matching the performance of human reviewers. Additionally, our analysis revealed that page edit history is a more effective indicator of low-quality content than contributor reputation, and we utilized our models to isolate and remove non-high-quality edits, thereby enhancing content indicator scores by an average of 15%.

Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable accuracy in a wide range of tasks, but their complex structure and the data they require make it difficult to adapt them to new situations. Most change detection methods based on deep learning need to be retrained whenever the class labels change, which can be costly and time-consuming. To address this limitation, we propose a new approach that allows knowledge to be transferred between models with different sets of classes. Our method involves two main components: extracting feature representations for existing models and using a common reference space, called an anchor space, obtained from additional, unrelated models. By projecting feature vectors from both the extraction model and a representation obtained through transfer learning, we can align them in a way that maximizes their correlation. Our results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional transfer learning techniques and compares favorably to perfect label transfer, with the added advantage of not requiring access to data from unrelated tasks.

A detailed analysis of reactions involving the $B^0_s$ meson has resulted in several significant discoveries. Firstly, the first observation of $B^0_s$ decaying into a $D^0$ and a $K^0_S$ was achieved, along with computing the branching ratio for this reaction as $3.4\pm0.7\pm0.4$ ppm. Secondly, the first evidence of $B^0_s$ decaying into a $D^0$ and a $K$ was found, along with computing its branching ratio as $1.1\pm0.5\pm0.2$ ppm. Lastly, the first observation of $B^0_s$ decaying into a $D^0$ and a $K$ was made, along with computing its branching ratio as $14\pm3\pm1$ ppm. These discoveries were made from $10^{11}$ $b\bar{b}$ pairs produced in proton-proton collisions at the LHCb experiment, which took place at a 13 TeV center-of-mass energy.

In the context of topological A-model string theory, a twisted cylinder serves as a fundamental object to derive T-duality rules, and we've undertaken a thorough examination of its properties and calculations of its key invariants. Our A-model invariants align perfectly with predictions from mirror symmetry, prompting us to suggest a new approach that connects these invariants to B-model calculations, specifically through two calculations of mixed homological algebra data.

Co-imitation is a type of social learning where an agent learns by observing another agent teaching multiple other agents, but there are challenges when the expert teacher isn't present. Our solution involves using co-imitation in a way that doesn't rely on the expert, enabling it to occur in both shared and separate environments. This approach allows the teacher to infer its own actions from the behaviors it sees in the students, making it possible for it to not be present. Our study shows that learning without the expert is more efficient as it, on average, requires fewer samples to replicate the same tasks as when the expert is present. Additionally, the average performance of the students using this method is better, showing it, on average, performs better as it, on average, achieves higher scores in the same tasks as when the expert is present.

This paper investigates properties of the Pascal metric, offering a thorough comparison with the Pascal-Laplace metric and deriving key results for Pascal universal lossless compression, including a universal lossless compression theorem and a construction of associated EFC codes. Interestingly, the achieved compression rate using PAC codes is found to be lower than that of the Laplace approach.

Understanding how humans interact with objects is crucial for comprehending human behavior and activities. However, accessing detailed information on human-object interactions in diverse settings is not very feasible. Our new dataset, the HIID, captures real-world sequences of humans manipulating multiple objects and makes this information accessible by tracking objects within 3D point cloud sequences. A novel model, the hand-centric tracker, enables accurate object tracking in these sequences, even in the presence of occlusions. Furthermore, we introduce a network to reconstruct how humans interact with objects, and another that can accurately recover individual object shapes in these sequences. Our model shows impressive results, and we analyze our dataset and evaluation protocols, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our object shape reconstruction network by achieving state-of-the-art performance on a new challenge of activity net object completion.

This study classifies C-groups with a specific structure - those that are non-crystallographic, have a Coxeter diagram with four components and an interleaving number of two. A total of 14 distinct families of such C-groups have been identified, comprising 11 novel ones. Additionally, an explicit form for the Weyl chamber and its boundary for a sub-set of these families has been derived, along with the formula for the Weyl group order.

A novel, markerless system for multi-axial robot depth camera depth calibration and end-effector pose estimation is proposed, utilizing a combination of a depth camera and visual features to determine positions without physical markers. A novel, robust and scale-invariant feature extraction method is designed to identify key points, calculate distances, and determine poses based on geometric relationships, reducing the system's dependence on lighting conditions and views. A learning-based end-effector pose estimation algorithm uses a regression neural network to predict accurate end-effector positions from calculated distances as input, eliminating the need for a calibrated world frame. Additionally, to compensate for the depth camera's limited field of view and viewing angle restrictions, a novel re-identification method restores the system's initial configuration when the end-effector is relocated. Our proposed system demonstrates high accuracy and robustness in real-world experiments, with comparison experiments showing its superiority over existing systems.

Researchers and policymakers face significant difficulties in distinguishing between interference effects and true therapy impacts, particularly when multiple concurrent interventions are administered. This challenge, known as therapy interference, has remained difficult to detect and quantify, resulting in inaccurate evaluations of individual therapies and inconclusive policy conclusions. Our study introduces a model capable of identifying nearby neighbors with negative interference, and develops an algorithm to detect potential cases. Using data from a large-scale randomized controlled trial in India, we applied this approach to analyze the effects of gold and antibiotic treatments for acute otitis media. Our results show that treating children with antibiotics and antibiotics found in the home significantly decrease follow-up visits, but eliminate the therapeutic benefits observed in the control group, effectively nullifying any advantage of the intervention.

In early solar models, particularly those of a young star, pseudoscalar-mediated Dark Matter annihilation within the core can interact with neutrons, resulting in enhanced emission of electron-neutrino and muon-neutrino pairs. This process, occurring at high velocities, is amplified by a factor of $v^2$ compared to its standard counterpart, where $v$ represents the neutron velocity. Furthermore, pseudoscalar annihilation into a DM pair, $AN^+A^-$, yields substantially increased emissions compared to the conventional SM annihilation channel, especially in smaller stellar bodies like neutron stars, where the neutrino energy released may far exceed that typically associated with photons. In a 10 solar mass young star model, under specific conditions, the energy from $v^2$-enhanced DM annihilation, produced by pseudoscalar parameters, can significantly contribute to the star's energy budget, with emitted neutrinos potentially accounting for up to 100 L$_{\odot}$ in luminosity.

The unambiguous identification of galaxy components is crucial for accurately measuring cosmic structure's evolution. We introduce ShapePipe, a cutting-edge pipeline that combines cutting-edge techniques, including model-based fitting, edge detection, and convolution-based methods, to precisely determine galaxy shapes. We assess ShapePipe's performance using three methods on both simulated and real data from the uncompleted UNIONS project and the CFIS, discovering that it surpasses existing methods in end-to-end shape measurement accuracy. Additionally, we employ ShapePipe to investigate weak lensing and cosmic shear effects, contributing to our understanding of these phenomena's role in UNIONS' shape catalog.

We establish enhanced, robust forms of the Kronecker-Weyl theorem and the Faltings-Weyl theorem for multiple variables, as well as extended robust forms of the Kronecker theorem and the Minkowski theorem for multiple variables. The derived outcomes have implications for the fields of uniform distribution and diophantine approximation, yielding refined versions of continued fraction approximations, as well as the Jarník theorem and the Gelfond theorem.

We prove that for complete varieties, being local Du Bois over a complete base is equivalent to being local rational in a complete base. This demonstrates the equivalence of two concepts: having local rational and local Du Bois singularities. Furthermore, if a variety has dimension 1 or 2, being Du Bois is equivalent to being rational, and for base dimension 3 or higher, being local rational and local Du Bois can both occur without being the same. We also establish some new local characteristics for variety singularities.

We've discovered a novel field-induced Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase in a spin-1/2 Heisenberg model system based on a single-crystal $\beta$-Cu$_2$O$_3$. We theoretically demonstrated that an external magnetic field applied in the (1,0,0) direction to this three-layer square Heisenberg model results in an effective two-dimensional J$_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model with antiferromagnetic J$_1$ and ferromagnetic J$_2$ interactions. We've also found that in this field-driven model there exists a broad temperature range of two-dimensional critical behavior that directly corresponds to the BKT phase in the standard J$_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model. Our findings are supported by numerical simulations using the cluster Monte Carlo method and our experimental results are in close agreement with these theoretical predictions, showcasing a stable physical BKT transition over a relatively broad temperature range.

This study investigates a hybrid of axion and sterile neutrino dark matter. The model features an axion, linked to a $P$-odd interaction, and a sterile neutrino, not linked to such an interaction, with dark matter becoming axion or sterile neutrinity depending on the energy scale. The transition to a non-perturbative regime, triggered by a quantum theta parameter, is governed by a first-order phase change. As a result, early dark matter is predominantly an axion, losing energy through a phase transition, with dark matter eventually transforming into a sterile neutrinity. Subsequently, a transition occurs at the QCD phase transition, transforming the axion dark matter into relativistic matter. Utilizing the relic abundance of dark matter, an analysis is performed to assess the feasibility of this model through a analysis of the model's parameters. The study shows that, for specific values of model parameters, the model accounts for the relic abundance of dark matter, with a resulting constraint on the sterile neutrino's mass being less than $5\times 10^{-6}$ eV. The model exhibits characteristics similar to a shadow matter, with a constraint on the axial interaction coupling constant being less than $5\times 10^{-6}$ eV.

Developing efficient quantum algorithms often relies on exact simulation methods,
with the key concept being the stabilizer rank of quantum states. The
stabilizer rank helps quantify how difficult it is to simulate a given state.
Previously, research limited the stabilizer rank for certain fractions of Pauli
terms in stabilizing a circuit. The new research improves this limit, applying it
to fractions of Pauli terms within any Pauli-sparse circuit, and achieves optimal
results for circuits containing a specific type of single-qubit gates. Additionally,
this work provides tight limits on the increase in stabilizer rank due to a
certain type of Pauli gate.

This research investigates the behavior of a complex form of essence model within a universe governed by Tsallis holographic dark energy, considering the two complex basis states of essence field parameters: $i\chi$ and $\chi + i\chi_1$. We evaluate the potential risks associated with the matter-dominated era by analyzing the future fate of the effective equation of state, as well as its stability, energy conditions, and statefinder diagnostics, represented by $D$ and $N$, respectively. Our analysis demonstrates that the universe's evolution towards a big rip big freeze scenario is contingent upon the type of essence model parameter it adheres to, with a universe containing Tsallis holographic dark energy and a complex form of essence model of type $i\chi$ eventually leading to a big rip big freeze scenario, whereas a type $\chi + i\chi_1$ model leads to a big freeze scenario, contrary to a real form of essence model which leads to a big rip scenario.

Data obtained from four $K$2 plates of the LAMOST Time-Domain Survey (LTDS) for the period of 2018 have been analyzed, with a total of 137399 spectra collected from 110237 unique stars, including 70009 in the complete sample and 40238 resulting from a incomplete sample due to various factors. The LTDS shows a substantial increase in its scientific scope compared to prior surveys, with a focus on nine main research areas and plans for a total of 1.3 billion spectra by the end of the project, set to significantly advance our comprehension in multiple scientific domains.

Recent years have seen a growing interest in using SRAM-based random number generators for security applications, such as the assignment of unbreakable identification codes. Prior research has indicated that DRS, a technique commonly used to optimize power consumption in processors, has the potential to produce high-entropy random numbers. Building on this finding, a novel TPG approach, the TuRaN algorithm, has been developed to effectively evaluate the SRAM-based RNGs' quality, taking into account their production variations and different operating conditions, including DR supply voltage. To validate the quality of the generated random numbers, the top-gate of the SRAM cell's access transistors is used to improve the RNG's entropy and ensure their reliability, as assessed through the application of NIST and die-hashing tests. The results show that TuRaN is a reliable method for verifying the SRAM-based RNGs' integrity, taking into account the impact of production variations and circuit design choices, and can effectively identify the optimal design choices for specific production batches.

A preconceived approach involves selecting an aligned, nonvolatile molecule that can act as a single-electron resistor switch by choosing a single atomic site for attachment to electroded substrates. This strategy focuses on single-electron circuits, comprising a single electron trap and a molecule. Through theoretical, computer-based simulations, it has been discovered that the cone-shaped redox molecules, like [Ru(bpy)2(dterpy)]2+, meet the requirements to act as single-electron resistor switches. These switches have been shown to possess specific properties, with a ratio of first to second Coulomb blockade tunneling energies of about 0.5 and an activation energy of roughly 800 millielectronvolts. Additionally, [Ru(bpy)2(dterpy)]2+ exhibits a significant on-off current ratio of about 10 for operation at an voltage of 0.45, has been found to possess a field effect, with a low switching threshold voltage of 0.35 volts, and has been determined to possess a figure of merit of about 320. These results suggest that the cone-shaped redox molecules are suitable for use as single-electron resistor switches.

The increasing precision required in particle physics means the need to numerically evaluate complex multi-loop Feynman integrals in principle. A novel approach to depict the topology of causal diagrams in complex momentum space is presented, using a spatial coordinate system to represent propagator dependence and worldlines for loop topologies. This causal depiction allows for the identification of loop structure and pinning, enabling multi-loop integrals to be computed by combining a set of nested sums with on-shell numerical factors in the Feynman parameter space. A software package, also known as CausalSpace, is developed to visualize these causal diagrams and compute the numerical values of general scalar massless Feynman integrals up to seven loops. The package features an interactive user interface that facilitates data entry, multi-loop integral computation, and a tabular display of results, complemented by a web interface for submitting pre-defined computation tasks.
